# 16b — Combat implementation plan

Draft 0.2, 2026-09-16, for [doc 16](16-combat-arena.md) Draft 0.2 on `main` at `5da8d6a`, revised after
the three-lens review in §10. Thirteen cuts, each with its steps, verify lenses and size, in the order
the dependencies allow. Sizes are approximate lines of production code plus tests.

---

## 0. Build discipline

1. Every cut ends with the workspace green: `cargo test --workspace --exclude mush-bot` plus
   `cargo test -p mush-bot` (the bot's exact-decimal JSON feature must not unify into the engine's test
   binaries), the contract gates blessed in the
   same commit that moves them (panic budget, state-slot owners, legacy-handler baseline, restriction
   lints census, module-namespace owners), all-target Clippy, and the story test and harness once they
   exist.
2. No second lane. A new capability extends the one that exists or replaces it in the same cut; nothing
   is kept "beside" for compatibility, because there is no data to be compatible with. The one shipped
   combat lane (`mush-sim::combat`) is retired by cut T (D-16-20).
3. No version ladders. A definition that changes is a new registry version with a migration chain; code
   carries one shape.
4. No fixture impersonates a production module. Tests compose the game crate's composition root, or drive
   `Arena::step` directly where no host is needed.
5. Each cut has a one-page design note in the ledger (§9) before it starts and an as-built entry when it
   lands, with the exact commands run. Reviews are performed by a reviewer that did not write the cut.
6. Panic policy: `panic → orderly exit`. The arena task's `catch_unwind` is the one place a panic is
   contained; it voids the match and commits nothing the faulted pulse touched, consistent with the
   world task's firewall.
7. Every new verb gets a non-baseline stanza in `crates/mush-contract-tests/legacy-handlers.toml` with a
   category and a note in the same commit; the pinned baseline only ever goes down.

### Load-sensitive test inventory (cut L, T-41)

The six suites first recorded as passing alone after failures in a loaded workspace run are
`mush-worldgen`'s `plan`, `review_plan`, and `s8_authority`; `mush-sim`'s
`journey::e7c6_b2`; and `mush-gateway`'s `two_process_e2e` and
`supervision_abandoned`. Later ledger entries also identify `mushd`'s `scripting_e2e`,
`mush-gateway`'s `server_panic_relaunch` and `restart_survival`, and `mushd`'s
`sim_reflex`. This is an investigation list, not permission to discard a failure: preserve the
first failure, establish its cause, and record both the whole-workspace and focused results.

The final cut L sweep also exposed an admission race in `mush-server`'s
`ipc_authoritative_action`: `tampered_offer_tag_is_rejected_before_intent` and
`authenticated_action_transfers_ownership_only_after_exact_intent` could receive `Busy`
before ownership. Their retry correction is recorded below; all eight tests in the
target passed focused validation at `02ead118` with normal test parallelism.
The Linux sweep at `5f8353b3` exposed the same pre-ownership race in
`actor_field_cannot_spoof_the_authenticated_connection` and
`a_peer_release_of_a_coordinator_action_cannot_kill_the_reader_loop`. It also
exposed socket-buffer assumptions in `mush-server`'s `ipc_teardown` and
`mushd`'s `load_soak`: both now observe detachment/timeout before draining.
The failures, fixture corrections and local/remote results are retained in the
[Cut L validation report](../reviews/cut-l-2026-09-22/validation.md).

Simulator integration waits in `mushd`'s `arena_story`, `arena_custody`, `observer_rule`,
`sim_cockpit`, `sim_lobby`, `sim_reflex`, `sim_rematch`, `sim_solo`, `sim_units`, and
`sim_weapons` use `tests/support::wait_until` for state transitions. Its deadline includes the
SSH or store read itself. Grace expiry waits for the named pilot's exact slot to read `left`
on the staff board, then asserts that reconnect does not restore cockpit control. The current
disconnect path releases focus and the arena binding but retains the human pilot's durable
billet until `EXIT` or check-in. The separate source-reviewed `B-81` in [16c](16c-simulator-backlog.md)
records explicit `+focus` and `STARTUP` admission after release: verified by reading at `8366b3fe`,
with no runtime probe and no established full control takeover; it is routed to cut B.4. Ledger checks
wait for the actual terminal event (`aborted` after `SIM ABORT`); movement premises use the
arena's reported clock.
Finite scripted firing sequences retain their explicit firing cadence and transient backoff.
The observer's provisional-phase tests load and select a test-owned sensor/unit pack with
`classify_after_ms = 15000`; the weapon, unit and rematch fixtures wait for the classified
callsign before retaining it across subsequent commands. The stock content stays unchanged.

## 2. Cut R: ruleset removal and base cleanup

**Goal.** One game, one sheet, one mechanic, one composition root; nothing that exists only to make a
second game possible.

### R-a (no deletion)

- R1. Hoist `mush-worldgen`'s structured-call machinery (`generate.rs` `generate_room` and
  `generate_brief`: forced tool, JSON-in-text fallback, repair round trip, typed validation,
  `prompt_hash`, priority, the `retryable | budget` error classification) into `mush-llm` as a generic
  `call_structured<T>`; re-point both worldgen sites to it. `ruleset-wod/src/st.rs`'s copy is not
  hoisted; it is deleted with its crate in R-b. `plan.rs`'s agentic loop is out of scope.
- R2. `git mv crates/ruleset-tacsim crates/tacsim`; add `composition.rs` and move into it:
  `server_modules`, `server_modules_with`, `tacsim_module`, `atlas_module`, `content_module`,
  `recovery_policy`, `run_module_migrations`, `SCHEMA_KEY`, `housing_title_issuer`,
  `market_title_issuer`, `org_capability_vocabulary` and `sim_routes.rs`; `mush-server/src/modules.rs`
  keeps host wiring and calls the game. Re-home `OnboardingConfig` into `mush-core`. Write down the
  new `tacsim` dependency list and add the `cargo tree -p tacsim` acyclicity test in the pattern of
  `mush-campaign` and `mush-industry`. Update `state_slot_owners.rs`'s `crate_family` (its
  `strip_prefix("ruleset_")` fallback) and every `ruleset_tacsim::` path in `config_ext.rs` (about 30).
- R3. `mush-ruleset` becomes a platform library: keep `schema`, `doc`, `store`, `chargen`, `render`,
  `vitals`, `interface`; delete the `Ruleset` trait's multi-implementation posture, `[rulesets].enabled`
  and `ruleset_modules`. `mush-tactics` keeps its `mush-ruleset` edge (it uses `pool_state`, `pool`,
  `vitals_frame`) and drops its dead `mush-dice` edge.

### R-b (the deletion)

- R4. The game sheet (`tacsim/src/sheet.rs`): `gunnery`, `piloting`, `sensors`, the character-first facts
  of doc 10 §17 to §19, the sheet verbs and chargen over the library. Size it against what
  `ruleset-wod/src/{schema, sheet_cmds, onboarding, state, roll, xp, agent, health, damage, chargen,
  chargen_cmds}.rs` provided (about 6k lines) and take only what the game needs now.
- R5. `mush-dice`: keep the expression evaluator for `+roll` and Rhai; delete `owod20` and `sr5`. The
  game's resolution (doc 16 §3.5) does not use it.
- R6. Economy and market: delete `SrCatalogSource`, `SrAvailability`, `SrDelivery`, `SrBoardObserver`,
  `vendor_caps`; give `housing_title_issuer` a game-owned id; rename `mush_housing::STORY_QUEUE` from
  `wod-story` to a neutral id and update `e5b.rs`; the `wod.usd` and `sr.nuyen` instruments go, the ten
  families arrive with cut C.
- R7. Delete `crates/ruleset-wod` and `crates/ruleset-shadowrun`; the `[wod]`, `[wod.economy]`,
  `[shadowrun]`, `[shadowrun.economy]` sections and their `Cfg` types; the WoD `ModuleAsync` arm in
  `world_task.rs`; `mush-market/src/record.rs`'s ruleset fields; `mush-npc`'s `wod_roll` and `sr_roll`
  abilities (one `check` ability over the game sheet replaces them) and the K8.4 providers
  `willpower_roll`, `willpower_set`, `condition_damage`, `condition_heal`.
- R8. Tests. Delete: `mushd/tests/{wod_e2e, wod_splats_e2e, wod_more_splats_e2e, shadowrun_e2e}.rs`
  and the two crates' suites. Re-point to the game sheet, never delete: the ruleset-specific cases in

  web_e2e, modules_e2e, support/mod}.rs`, `mush-server/tests/{e7r2_proving_loop,
  h2c_ability_coordinator, market_issuer, production_action_migrations, boot_parity,
  provisioning_smoke, e4c_bridge, e6b_seal}.rs`, the four TUI goldens (`tui_sheet`, `tui_rolls`,
  `tui_damage`, `tui_vitals_two_feeds`) and the `mush-proto/tests/wire.rs` and `mush-core/src/lock.rs`
  fixtures. Rewrite as one-sheet tests: `mush-contract-tests/tests/{vitals_projection_clean,
  npc_ability_residual, legacy_handler_allowlist, state_slot_owners}.rs`.
- R9. Gates, in the same commit: remove the 49 ruleset stanzas from `legacy-handlers.toml` and lower

that proved a platform property with WoD content still passes with the game sheet; `onboarding_e2e`,

## 6. Cut A: the arena core library

`crates/tacsim/src/arena/`:

- A1. `state.rs`: `Arena`, `ArenaDefinition`, `UnitState`, the epoch table, the shadow contact store, the
  due-event heap, the ledger egress ring.
- A2. `clock.rs`: tempo states, thresholds, hysteresis, `dt` clamping, `Lagged`, the substep length.
- A3. `intents.rs`: `Control` application, apply-time authorisation against the epoch table, continuous
  latest-wins, discrete sequenced and bounded.
- A4. `motion.rs`: doc 16 §3.4 per substep over `move_cost`; `index.rs`: the uniform grid.
- A5. `rng.rs`: `draw(seed, label)` and the enumerated labels; `hash.rs`: the per-substep state hash;
  `ledger.rs`: events, chunking, bounds, position summaries.
- A6. `step.rs`: the five phases of doc 16 §3.1 in order, each documented with its snapshot rule.
- A7. Tests: unit tests per module; the cross-tempo property test (one scripted intent and control log at
  5,000, 1,000 and 500 ms yields one event list and one hash sequence, crossing an impassable band and an
  occupied cell); a test that a tempo change mid-run changes no outcome; a test that adding a draw label
  shifts no existing draw.

**Verify lenses.** The arena module has no `use mush_store`, `tokio`, `GatewaySink` or `&mut World`;
`step` is `&mut self` over the inputs and nothing else; the harness at 300 moving units stays under
5 ms per pulse before perception and weapons exist.

**Size.** About 3.5k lines plus 2.5k tests.

## 7. Cut T: the arena task, the seam, custody, and the old lane's retirement

- T0. Disposition of the shipped lane (D-16-20): delete `mush-sim/src/combat.rs`'s verbs (`+fire
  +launch +heading +thrust +posture +dc +dock +eject`), the `tactical_intent` staging, the placeholder
  resolution in `tick.rs`, `s9_fire_gate.rs`, and the `+fire` stanza in `legacy-handlers.toml`
  (lowering the baseline). The `domaintick` pulse and `DomainTickCommit` remain for world-side
  non-combat domains; add a test that a `deployed` unit is never a participant of a world-side pulse.
- T1. `arena_task.rs`: owns an `Arena`, the inbox (`intents.max_pending_per_unit`), the egress ring
  (`ledger.max_unflushed_chunks`, the per-pilot frame slots), a timer driven by `next_due_ms`, a
  watchdog (`tempo.stall_ms`), `catch_unwind` around `step`, a `watch::Sender<bool>` stop signal, a
  `JoinHandle` on `PersistHandles` joined in both shutdown tails.
- T2. Custody. Check-out on `Boarding → Running` as one authoritative action: the `deployed { arena,
  snapshot }` marker on each unit record; refusals added with one shared helper at
  `TacticsDestroyGate::check`, `TacticsDetachGate::check`, `unit_damage`, `unit_remove` and the
  `@spatial` move commands; the world placement left frozen; `CustodyOut` sent. Check-in per unit,
  fallible: cells through `apply`, pose through `mush_sim::place`, `custody_lost` for a vanished unit;
  marker cleared; tank reset; seats, leases, focus and pods released. `Void` restores snapshots.
- T3. Routing: the cockpit verbs (cut K) validate focus, lease and epoch on the world task and forward
  `Intent`s; `Control` on seat activation, deactivation, revocation, linkdead onset and revival, `EXIT`,
  `SIM ABORT`; `Stop` on abort, timeout and void.
- T4. Output: the world task drains the arena's frame slots each iteration and emits them through its
  ordinary output path as `SendTarget::Char`; the arena has no `GatewaySink` and no session view.
  Ledger chunks are appended by the world task to `log:match.<id>` through `mush_core::Ledger` on its
  lane.
- T5. Boot reconciliation in the tactics recovery pass: `deployed` markers with no live arena are
  restored from snapshot, cleared, and their seats, leases, focus and pods released, with an
  `aborted(restart)` result.
- T6. `mush-contract-tests`: the arena library has no path to `ObjectStore`, `WriteBatch`,
  `GatewaySink` or `&mut World` (a source scan in the style of `restriction_lints`); the draw-label set
  is pinned; the custody markers are the only unit writes during a match.

**Verify lenses.** A `mushd` test and a gateway test board two fake pilots, start a match, drive, and end
by abort; unit records are byte-identical before check-out and after check-in when nothing happened,
and a unit driven ten cells has its world placement at the arena's final pose; a panic injected into
`step` voids the match with reason and the world keeps serving commands; a server restart mid-`Running`
leaves the units mutable and the pods free.

**Size.** About 3k lines plus 2k tests.

---

## 8. Cuts C, K, S, W, N, X

**Cut C, content and registry.**
- C0. The atlas `item` decoder gains `interior: bool`, applied as an interior space at pack apply; the
  eight pod items use it.
- C1. Typed decoders in `tacsim/src/definitions/` for units, weapons, ammunition, sensors, resolution
  tables and arenas; registration through the C1 registry as `RulesDefinition` entries.
- C2. `neighborhood.ooc_area.json` to version 4 in `mush-atlas`: `room_budget.maximum` raised to 10,
  the simulator lobby, red room and blue room, their exits, the selector item and the eight pods; the
  digest pin in `starter.rs` re-blessed. A test applies the upgrade on a world at version 3 and on a
  fresh world.
- C3. `content/arenas/proving_ground.json`: the 2.56 km arena with authored tiles, entry zones, key
  spots, the waypoint graph and the eight tank objects' initial placements; the tanks are created once
  by the arena pack's applier.
- C4. `content/resources.json`: the ten commodity families as `InstrumentDef` rows, registered at boot.
- Verify: the packs load on a fresh world and on a world at `ooc_area@3`; every definition has an exact
  version and validates its references.

**Cut K, cockpit and lobby.**
- K1. `match/` state machine with the named `Boarding → Running` trigger, `SIM` verbs, slots, `SIM
  START`, `SIM ABORT`, `match.max_duration_ms`, atomic release, the reset to `Idle`.
- K2. `BOARD` through `Transition::Place Interior`, the tank's station assignment,
  `request_seat_activation` with `helm`, `sensors`, `fire`, focus; `EXIT`.
- K3. Cockpit verbs as contextual selectors; `STARTUP` with the `power` capability and its due event;
  `VIEW`, `STATUS`, `WEAPONSTATUS`, `CONTACTS` frames.
- K4. Linkdead onset and revival delivered as `Control`; reclaim at a pulse boundary with a new epoch;
  the idle substitution recorded.
- Verify: two fake pilots complete `Selection → Boarding → Running → Aborted → Idle` twice in a row; a
  third account cannot claim a taken slot; a pilot who types `FIRE` then `EXIT` in one burst fires
  nothing; a pilot who disconnects mid-match reclaims on reconnect.

**Cut S, perception.**
- S1. Sensor and signature definitions; the pass (`arena/perception.rs`) as a due event over the index
  and the atlas trace with per-unit `Eye` heights; classification with the gap rule; team sharing.
- S2. The shadow contact store, id minting, the one refusal; contacts mirrored into the pilot's frame.
- S3. Notices with hysteresis; the world-side exclusion of the arena domain from `visible_rooms`,
  `units_for`, `+map`, `look` and unit listings; `unit.status` for deployed units.
- Verify: the observer rule surface by surface (cockpit, `+map`, `look`, `@unit/status`, notices, TUI,
  web); the harness's candidates, traces and probes per pulse.

**Cut W, weapons, resolution, damage.**
- W1. Weapon and ammunition definitions, `LOCK`, `FIRE` with cycle and ammunition, the percentage.
- W2. Resolution per doc 16 §3.5 over `direct_fire_path` and the silhouette tables; scheduled impacts as
  due events; revalidation; the blocked shot as a costed miss.
- W3. Damage as `UnitMutationPlan` through `apply`; consequences; wrecks; team elimination ending the
  match.
- W4. **The story test** in `mushd/tests/arena_story.rs` and its gateway twin.
- Verify: the story test; a shot at a target behind full cover costs a round and a cycle and misses; a
  moving target that leaves the predicted cell misses with reason; ammunition is conserved across a
  match; the money rule.

**Cut N, reflex AI and the cost run.**
- N1. The state machine controller and utility target choice in `arena/reflex.rs`; the waypoint graph;
  `[atlas].path_max_cells` raised for the arena; the `unreachable` edge; path queries bounded per pulse.
- N2. The harness drives all 300 units through it; `Engaged` p99 under 25 ms.
- N3. The deliberation hook: the order type, squad grouping, the decision pipeline request with a TTL,
  the doctrine fallback; the cost run mode behind `TACSIM_LLM_COST_RUN=1`.
- Verify: the harness thresholds; the cost run produces its table when the owner runs it.

**Cut X, extensions.** One cut per item of doc 16 §9, each adding its acceptance test and touching no
existing test.

The compensating `ServiceReq::UnlinkPlayer { character }`, `ServiceResp::UnlinkPlayer(bool)`, `WorldMsg::UnlinkPlayer` (classed `WorldRead`) and `WorldHandle::unlink_player` are sent from both failed `store.link_character` arms: `Accounts::create_and_link` through `forget_character`, and `run_newchar`. `mush_sim::on_obj_destroyed` unlinks a destroyed character through `AccountOracle::unlink`. `SimError::UnknownAccount` now reads "This character has no account on record, so the simulator cannot hold a slot for it." **The layer switch.** `deploy/dev1` and `deploy/dev2` write `[tacsim]` with `enabled = true` ahead of the dotted blocks. `mushd.toml.example`, `mushd.toml.tmpl` and `instance.env.example` say that the flag instantiates the simulator. `lobby::require_layer` is the first line of `claim`, `leave`, `start`, `abort`, `status_lines` and `cockpit::board`, and answers the new `SimError::LayerOff`. `SimError::NoUnit` names the boot log, not a re-apply that no verb performs. The brief names only the subcommands that claim, start or board, and the design note says `SIM START` names the cause. A healthy-looking board over a server with no arena is the defect the finding describes. (2) `SimGate` is deleted outright, not given a stand-aside arm, and its `match_::SimGate` re-export is gone. With the stand-aside it would decide nothing, and `sim_command` gives the same `OUTSIDE_CENTRE` line from the command table, where exit and player aliases get their turn first. As a consequence, `sim wibble` and a bare `SIM TEAM` outside the centre now print usage and "Which side?" before any location check. (3) The shared map is reached through two default-`false` mutators on the `AccountIdentity` trait and a `std::sync::RwLock`. The brief suggested "no lock". Both readers already hold the one `Arc<dyn AccountIdentity>`, `&self` on a shared `Arc` needs interior mutability, and a fixed test oracle now refuses a write it would otherwise drop. (4) `account` is an `Option` on the wire. `None` means the id could not be minted; the character then stays unmapped and fails closed, and both halves log it. This avoids turning an unreachable mint failure into a hard account-creation failure. (5) A second wire variant at the same `IPC_VERSION` 6, `ServiceReq::UnlinkPlayer` with `ServiceResp::UnlinkPlayer`, was added by the fixer. Without it the RAM insert would outlive a failed `store.link_character`. It is classed `IngressClass::WorldRead`, because it touches the oracle only and can only make a policy fail closed. If it is refused mid-commit, the mapping stands until the next boot, which is logged. No staff relink verb exists, so none was covered. The legacy `accounts.json` import needed nothing, because it runs before `hydrate`. (6) A poisoned map lock keeps answering reads from the intact table and refuses both writers. An empty table would silently unmap every character on the server. (7) The readiness line is logged from `mush-server/src/boot.rs` after `boot_modules`, through the new `centre::readiness`. It is not logged from tacsim's own `on_world_loaded`, because the content module composes after tacsim, so a first boot has no rooms or roster there yet. (8) The muster rows were taken exactly as suggested: 97, 93, 101 and 89. Slot 4's row 89 is therefore outside the ford band (rows 92 to 102), and its straight run still meets deep water. Only slot 1's run is asserted. The muster nodes went to row 105. (9) The arena pack's `note` was rewritten, not appended to, because `ArenaDef.note` is capped at 1,024 bytes. Deploy: `deploy/dev1-split/deploy.sh` step 0 refuses, before the service user and everything after it, a missing `web/dist/index.html` or one older than any file under `web/src`, naming `npm ci && npm run build`, and `GATEWAY_RESTART=1` turns the already-up reload into `systemctl restart`; `deploy/dev1-split/README.md` builds the SPA before the cargo builds in both recipes, tables which crates mean restart and not reload, and gives a build-elsewhere recipe; `deploy/README.md`, `docs/help/cockpit.md` (a per-client screen-0 section), `web/README.md` and the fixtures `README.md` follow. **Q.6** (`c3774cd4`): Built on `6bde3c4b`, +2,430/-76 over 16 tracked files, no new file. **Motion carries.** `arena/state.rs`: `pub struct MotionCarry { turn: u32, speed: u32, east: i64, north: i64 }` (re-exported from `arena::`) and `UnitState.carry`, set to `default()` by the one `UnitState` literal in `Arena::new`, and written only by `motion::integrate`. `arena/motion.rs`: `pub const DISTANCE_SCALE: i64 = 1_000 * SIN_ONE` (1,048,576,000), private `RATE_SCALE = 1_000`, `scale_round` deleted, new private `fn axis(speed_cms, dt, fixed, carry) -> i64`. `turn` takes `budget = turn_rate_mdeg_s x dt + carry.turn`, steps `(budget / 1000).min(arc)` and keeps `budget % 1000`, zeroing the carry when the arc closes, when there is no arc, on a forbidden side, and on the wreck, dead-engine or cold return. `accelerate` does the same with `carry.speed`, zeroed at `target == current` and when the clamp lands on the target; its wreck, dead-engine or cold return also zeroes `east` and `north`. Travel per axis is `num = speed_cms x dt x sin_fx or cos_fx + carry`, then `div_euclid` and `rem_euclid` by `DISTANCE_SCALE` with every multiplication saturating, so reverse carries as forward does. The no-whole-centimetre early return is now `east == 0 && north == 0`, taken AFTER the carries are banked, so a 3 cm/s crawl accumulates. The off-window refusal and `stop_at_boundary` (every `BlockedCause`: `Impassable`, `Occupied`, `TooSteep`, `Edge`) zero `speed`, `east` and `north` with the speed; `carry.turn` is deliberately not a stop's business. `arena/hash.rs`: the four carries are folded per unit after `grade_pct` as `u32`, `u32`, `i64`, `i64` LE, as doc-list item 13, so every hash in every match moves from substep 0; no absolute hash is pinned anywhere. The module head states what is exact however arena time is cut (a straight run at constant speed, a pure turn, a ramp on uniform ground) and what is not (position while accelerating or turning-and-moving is first-order, semi-implicit Euler; event timestamps are substep boundaries; the absolute lattice is not taken). **The substep bound.** `Clock::substep_ms` is `min(substep_max_ms, (cell_cm - 1) x 1000 / max_speed_cms)` floored at `MIN_SUBSTEP_MS`, with the free function delegating. The pinned 200 becomes 199, the only existing assertion that changed in the tree. Its doc re-derives that one axis of travel, carry included, is at most `cell_cm - 1`, and says this is margin and not repair. The stock tank stays cap-bound at 250 ms, so no shipped partition moved. **The honest hit count.** In `resolve_impact` the `state.hits` increment moved inside `if !plan.ops().is_empty()`. `UnitReturn.hits` and `UnitResult.hits` now count rounds that took something off something, and their docs say this is not the ledger's count of `hit` lines; the `hit` line, `section_destroyed` and the pilot's notice are unchanged. **The jammed mesh (W6 closed).** `share_pass` folds `jamming_at(..).map(recovered(own eccm))` at the sharer once per pass and at each mate. A link needs `sees` at the TIGHTER of the two `budget(attenuation)` values and `range_cm <= min` of the two `scale(reach)` values, using the sensor pass's own four functions. A stock match pays nothing: `jam_radius_cm == 0` returns before the index or a counter, and `in_range` decides with `within_cm`, which is exactly `range_cm <= r`. `arm_boot_sweep`'s doc records why the sweep stays on the first tick (no post-load `Module` hook). **Tests.** In-source `motion.rs`: a `drive` harness over `clock::substeps` and `PARTITIONS` of (5000,250), (5000,150), (5000,50), (370,250). `the_carries_make_a_run_a_turn_and_a_ramp_independent_of_the_substep` pins a crawl at exactly +300 cm, a run at +4,000 cm, a turn at 133,332 mdeg and a ramp at 666 cm/s at all four. `one_obstacle_is_one_stop_at_every_partition` pins the same centimetre 3,999, held, the pilot told once, and prints the ledger counts. `a_unit_at_the_edge_of_its_cell_at_full_speed_is_never_refused` pins 199 at both 5,000 and 4,999 cm/s, no stop in 60 s, and end poses of exactly 999 + 300,000 and 999 + 299,940 with a rolling carry. `a_stop_a_wreck_and_a_cold_hull_all_zero_the_carries` is driven at 30,000 mdeg so both axes carry into each of the four causes. `hash.rs`: `the_hash_folds_each_of_the_four_motion_carries`. `tests/extensions.rs` gained a `q6_` rig (`q6_window`, `q6_arena`, `Q6Replay::lines`, `q6_replay`, `q6_three_cadences`, `q6_share`, `q6_mesh_arena`, `q6_meshed`, `q6_fit_filter`). It holds the four owed cross-tempo tests at 5,000/1,000/500 ms with one event list, one per-substep hash sequence and one final state: X.2 the leg fight, with a halfway property proving the pair rule fires on the second leg; X.3 the thermal watch separating cold, idling and under way; X.4 found-lost-found through a bubble; X.5 the filtered twin never losing it. It also holds five mesh tests (pod beside the receiver by range, by budget, pod beside the SHARER at both terms, cold or wrecked pod, `jam_checks == 0` on a pod-free field) and the mandatory `q6_one_scripted_jammed_share_at_three_cadences_is_one_event_list`. `resolution.rs`: the spent-section test reads `(shots_fired, hits)` at all three cadences and asserts `hits == hit lines - rounds on the spent section` and `shots_fired == 8`. **The owner's ruling of 2026-09-20** (a lock taken on `X1` continues when the contact becomes `BA`), with no behaviour change needed, is pinned at three levels. `weapons.rs` (j): the same `ContactId`, the frame's lock `Provisional(1)` then `Slot { Blue, 1 }`, the gunner's whole notice list `["classified"]`, zero `lost` or `lock_lost`, one `locked` line even after a repeated `Lock` intent, and a `FIRE` with no re-lock resolving against the same target. `cockpit.rs` (new `Rig::frame`): `LOCK BA`, `ba`, `X1` and `x1` all answer `Locking BA.` with the frame's lock unmoved, and `RANGE`, `BEARING`, `WEAPONSTATUS` and `SCAN` with no argument name `BA` and never the sixteen digits. `sim_weapons.rs`: over SSH the word the lock was taken under still resolves after the rename and `WEAPONSTATUS` still reads `Locked on`. Harness new baseline at seed 2350: p99 8.19 ms against the 12 ms ceiling, `substep_ms=250`, blocked 250 to 288, moving_at_end 87 to 97, path_cells 133,304 to 170,558, hits 699 to 702, wrecks 16 to 14, ledger_bytes 1,427,063 to 1,407,410, peak traces 2,486, peak share_ops 210, every counter reproduced byte for byte by three builds. No gate, pack version, verb, draw label, frame field, wire key or player sentence moved; `panic_budget/tacsim.txt` stays 3. **Q.7** (`b553eaf0`): AI fill is playable (built on `c3774cd4`; +3,770/-112 over 29 tracked files plus the new `crates/mushd/tests/sim_solo.rs`, 629 lines). **Blocked learned at the event.** `arena/reflex.rs` gains `Arena::note_blocked(unit, cell, cause, t_ms)`. `substep` feeds it on the same rising edge that journals `EventKind::Blocked`, collected inside the units borrow and applied after `now_ms` advances and before the due loop, so the remembered stamp is the ledger line's own `t_ms` and that substep's `ReflexTick` already knows. It is a no-op unless the unit is under `Controller::Reflex` with a machine. It always clears `route`. For `BlockedCause::Occupied` alone it also clears `searched_ms` and pushes the cell onto the new hashed `ReflexUnit.avoid: Vec<((u16,u16), i64)>`; a repeat refreshes its stamp in place, which keeps it idempotent per cell as Q.6 warned, and the oldest entry drops at `REFLEX_AVOID_MAX = 8`. `decide` drops entries at `REFLEX_AVOID_TTL_MS = 30_000` at the top of every tick and never on a goal change. `ReflexMemory::adopt` into a new state clears `avoid` and the three new Withdraw fields. The old `if unit.blocked { route.clear() }` edge is deleted. `path::path_with` gains `avoid: &[(u16,u16)]`: an avoided cell is skipped after the passability test, an avoided goal is an ordinary `NoRoute`, and `path` passes `&[]`. `shoulder_refuses` becomes `pub(crate)`. **The follower.** With no route, `follow` steers at the goal only when `first_step_is_open` passes. That test takes the octant of the bearing through `octant_step` and requires the neighbour to be on the window, `passable()`, not in `avoid`, and open by `edge_is_open` (`slope::too_steep` and, on a diagonal, `shoulder_refuses`). Otherwise `plan.speed_cms = Some(0)` with no heading. The wandered-off-route branch also clears `searched_ms`. **Withdraw is not terminal.** New hashed `stand_until_ms`, `quiet_since_ms` and `rallied`, the constant `REFLEX_STAND_TICKS = 3`, and the key `[tacsim.arena.reflex].rally_ms = 20000`, plumbed through `ReflexConfig`, `TacsimReflexCfg`, `config_ext`, the example, the instance template and dev2. A dry edge into `Withdraw`: `is_dry` = `UnitState::armed_at_checkout()` and no weapon row with rounds, taken whether or not the unit has rallied, and such a unit never rallies. The health edge is not taken by a `rallied` unit. An `Objective::Withdraw` order still overrides. Inside the state, `withdraw_stand` refuses a dry unit and one under `hold_fire`. Otherwise it takes `best_hostile`'s classified candidate, tests the plot range against `order_reach_cm`, then pays one `reflex_has_line` trace. A stand sets `stand_until_ms = t + 3 × decide_ms`, zero speed and the heading onto the plot, and calls `engage_orders`, with `goal`, `route` and `target` untouched. The dwell holds the unit stopped until the stamp passes. The rally runs when the unit has arrived (within `ARRIVE_CELLS` of its goal, or has no goal) and `holds_a_hostile` is false and it is not dry: `quiet_since_ms` runs to `rally_ms`, then the unit goes to `Patrol` with `rallied = true`. A released seat rallies by the same rule. **Heat.** `engage_orders` skips a weapon when `would_overheat` says so. That is the engine's own line: no `heat` cell never holds a shot back, `now >= max` refuses, and otherwise the test is `now + per_shot > max`. **`EndReason::Spent`** (wire word `spent`). `Arena::spent` is true when both teams are present, each has an in-action unit that was armed at check-out, no in-action unit has a round left, and no `DueKind::Impact` is pending. `Arena::settle_spent` runs immediately after `settle_elimination` at both sites. It maps to `MatchState::Ended`, `MatchOutcome::Draw` and `reason_word` "spent". `MatchOutcome`'s six words are unchanged. `Centre.outcome_reason` carries the reason through `on_match_finished(…, reason)`, and the board prints `ended (match N) — draw: both sides are out of ammunition`. `hash.rs` folds the avoid count as `u64`, then each entry's two `u16` and its `i64` stamp, then two `fold_stamp`s and the `rallied` byte. **One human against the fill.** With `ai_fill` on, `lobby::start` needs one claimed slot in the centre (`NobodyPlaying` is the guard). `run` refuses a centre with nobody seated and tops each side up to `ai_side_size`. It takes the lowest unclaimed pods that have a tank, as `Fielded { unit, slot: index }`. `settle_boarding` and `board_deadline` abort only an empty centre, with the sentences `… nobody is left to fly it.` and `… nobody boarded.` `Centre.ai_side_size: Option<u8>` is a floor: `ai_side_size = stored.unwrap_or(0).max(largest_side).clamp(1, slots_per_side)`. It is cleared at `Idle`. `SIM AI [n]` is the sixth `Selector` (`Selector::Ai`, word `ai`): lead or staff, `Selection` only. The new refusals are `AiOff`, `AiRange` and `AiBelowSide`. The read sentence is `AI fill: N a side.` and the set sentence is `AI fill set to N a side.` A non-numeric argument answers ``How many a side? `SIM AI 2`.`` The board says ` AI fill: each side fields N; machines take the unclaimed pods.` in `Selection`, `Boarding` and `Running`. With `ai_fill` off both refusals and both abort sentences stand byte for byte. The template and dev2 turn `ai_fill` on; the example stays off. **Config values.** `ArenaConfig::validate`, `MatchConfig::validate`, `SensorsConfig::validate` and `HarnessConfig::validate` are pure functions with thirty rules. Messages take the shape `[tacsim.arena.tempo].engaged_ms must be at least 50 (it is 0)`. They are called only from `config_ext::tacsim_config`, before `verify_sources`, and never from `Arena::new`. The owner's lock-survives-rename ruling needed no code; Q.6's `cockpit.rs` pin stands. **Q.8** (`f90113c3`): Extension units in the centre. `content::fielded_sources()` is `sources()` followed by `EXTENSIONS`, `EXTENSIONS_BIPED`, `EXTENSIONS_THERMAL`, `EXTENSIONS_ECM`, `EXTENSIONS_ECCM` (ten packs, `requires` order, named `<built-in ...>`). `Catalog::build_game`'s body is factored into a private `build_from(base, operator, owner)`, and `pub Catalog::build_fielded` builds over the fielded sources. The three production sites now call it: `tacsim::builtin_definitions`, `TacsimRuleset::register` and `TacsimStore::install_packs`. `build_game` stays the stock game with no production caller, and no `build_game` test moved. The fielded catalog adds exactly units `tacsim.unit.{line_tank_laser, biped_mk1, line_tank_thermal, line_tank_ecm, line_tank_eccm}`, weapon `laser_mk1`, ammunition `laser_charge` and sensors `thermal_mk1`, `ecm_mk1`, `eccm_mk1`. Every stock `DefinitionRef` is pinned unmoved, and nothing new is latched (`boot_packs()` is still the atlas pack then the arena pack). `build_from`'s duplicate rule is now digest-aware: an operator pack under a shipped `(id, version)` is skipped when its declared digest is the shipped one and refused by file name with both digests when it is not. The cause is cut F.2's two-flag split: `step.rs` journals on the rising edge of the per-substep `blocked` flag and tells the pilot on the rising edge of `held`. The carry that would close the gap is the one a refusal must not bank. The test asserts what is true (the same centimetre, held, the pilot told once at all four partitions) and prints the counts with only `>= 1` asserted. The remedy (gate the journal on `!was_held`, and fold `held` into `state_hash`) changes what the hash covers and is deferred to a ruling before Q.7. A stop is therefore NOT one `Blocked` ledger event at every substep length, and Q.7's blocked-cell memory must be idempotent per cell or read the `held` edge; the Q.6 brief's closing paragraph said the opposite. (2) Doc 16 §3.1's substep formula becomes `(cell_cm - 1) x 1000 / max_speed_cms`. The brief's stated reason (a carry rollover making a two-cell step under the old bound) is arithmetically false: `cell_at` divides and the carry is inside the one quotient, so the old bound was also one cell. A Held line ends a leg, a fresh live hostile ends the hunt, and a kill (`{d} destroyed.`, or `Target destroyed.` of the lock) drops the trail and adds the designator to a per-match `wrecks` set that `target()`, the hunt's gates and the quiet timer all skip, so a still-listed wreck is never locked, orbited, shot, hunted or counted. **The held tank.** A Held notice records `held_from_deg`, turns `HELD_TURN_DEG` for `HELD_FOR_MS` and re-sends the speed as insurance. The stall watchdog, judged once per new STATUS read and `STALL_MS` apart, turns 90, 135 and 180 degrees from the stop heading, held against the doctrine, then backs off at `-max_astern` for `HELD_REVERSE_MS`; a new stop resets it, and a free read clears `held_from_deg`. **The fire clock.** `Weapon.next_ready_ms` is the one clock `believed_ready` reads (the `fired_ms + cycle_ms` path removed). `Weapon.slack_ms` starts at `FIRE_SLACK_START_MS`, is lowered by each ack toward `FIRE_SLACK_MIN_MS` 500 (one engaged pulse) and raised by `FIRE_SLACK_UP_MS` on a `Still cycling` answer to the runner's own FIRE, capped at `FIRE_SLACK_MAX_MS`, with a const assert on the order. The ack sets the clock to ack plus the learned cycle plus the slack; a `cycling` row or refusal to its reading time plus the whole seconds plus the slack; an accepted ready row to its own time; a paired arena refusal that is not cycling to now. `Picture::sent_fire(now_ms, weapon)` keeps marks per weapon, matched by id or short name. **The lock fix.** Its base sigma is 10, 20 or 50 by plot age. **Notes and records.** `Pilot::take_notes` sentences drained by `Lane::tick` into `LaneEvent::Said`; `picture_json` gains `pilot { hunt: null or { d, leg, age_s }, fallen_back, stall }`; `Lane::pilot()`; thirteen tunable constants named with their bounds in the module head. **Tests.** 20 new pilot tests, 7 new picture tests, 1 settings test and 4 lane tests on a scripted server grown with `pulse_ms`, `magazine` and `held` (a `HeldKnob`) knobs, all off by default and set through `to_the_fight_with`. ### Cut L — design note (2026-09-22, before implementation)

Base: `origin/main` at `145296c2`. Scope is 16c cut L, independently of AA and B.
The operator can lift a password tempban through the store, preserve the SSH host
identity during a reset, bootstrap the first staff account without hand-written
Redis data, and distinguish authentication refusal from token cool-off. Config,
operator logs, repository documentation and CI must describe the one current game.

**Owner clarification.** The owner confirmed dev2 is unused and authorized its
removal (2026-09-22). Remove the repository's bespoke dev2 deployment/config/test
lane; another testing instance uses the shared instance template. This supersedes
Q31's prerequisite for an SSH inspection. No live instance is reset or removed by
this implementation.

**Boundaries.** L.1 owns operator/authentication paths, reset/deploy scripts and
boot diagnostics. Tempban lifts are time-limited store commands consumed once by
each connection-owning guard, preserving newer bans and permanent sitebans. Staff
bootstrap uses the existing account/store authority, validates credentials, never
prints a password/hash, and refuses a nonempty account store. Transport admission
hooks become required, and token cool-off gets its own websocket close code.
First-boot pack refusal is fatal: `on_world_loaded` already returns `ModError`, so
propagate the original cause through the normal boot firewall and fail tests at
boot rather than later on a missing room. This follows L's fail-boot option.

L.2 adds omitted config keys, warns about a disabled simulator and pod-count
clamping, detects likely misspelled top-level sections, removes dev2 and retires
the deleted ruleset-selector names. The naming-only edits precede e2e wait changes.
L.3 corrects current docs without changing the combat timing or lease contract;
three-channel K6 leases still wait for a second station (Q33).
L.4 adds strict rustdoc, built-SPA release/TLS checks and env-gate inventory, and
changes simulator waits to bounded observable conditions while preserving their
assertions. The cost run remains opt-in and requires no paid provider for CI.

**Verification.** Focused auth/CLI/store, provisioning, shipped-config and
simulator tests first; then formatting, all-target Clippy, contract gates,
`cargo test --workspace --exclude mush-bot`, the separate bot suite, the story
and harness, strict workspace rustdoc, and the built-SPA release binaries.
Linux CI verifies shell/systemd-shaped fixtures. Independent review precedes
integration; refresh main and rerun affected gates after resolving conflicts.
Existing physics/delivery findings remain AA's and are not bundled into L.

**As built (2026-09-22): L.1–L.4 complete and validated; integration record
[PR #1](https://github.com/faenix7/rustmush/pull/1).** The frozen Linux run uses `5f8353b3`; `fbe91f75` adds
six test-file corrections. Final source `ffa12f6b` also incorporates AA.3's two
production files and one test file, making the validation overlay nine files.
Detailed results and retained failures are in the
[validation report](../reviews/cut-l-2026-09-22/validation.md). `@siteban/lift` publishes a
five-minute store command with a fresh
request ID and issuance cutoff. Each connection-owning guard consumes it once,
preserving newer password failures and permanent sitebans. ID creation belongs
to the store-domain constructor, outside provider implementation files.
Admission hooks are required. Websocket token cool-off upgrades and closes with
`4429`, retaining the credential for retry; invalid credentials still use
`4401`. Match boarding and `Running` transitions log at INFO, closed SSH
connections cancel their pre-auth watchdog, disabled deliberation logs at DEBUG,
and stdout uses ANSI only on a terminal.

`--bootstrap-staff <account>` on `mushd` and `mush-server` reads a bounded
password line from redirected stdin, uses normal recovery and world boot, holds
the instance lock, starts no listener, and atomically refuses an existing account
store. Neither password nor hash is printed or accepted on argv.
`reset-instance.sh --staff` uses that path and preserves `ssh_host_ed25519`.
Successful SPA builds stamp their source commit; deploy requires that exact
commit and `index.html`, including from `git archive`.

Shipped configs expose ground-cell size, ephemeris and path-search bounds, with
required-section and explicit-value gates. Disabled TacSim logs WARN; a ceiling
above the four authored pods logs its clamp once at centre readiness. Unknown
top-level sections within two edits of known names are refused; unrelated
extensions remain allowed. Selector names became `sheet_modules` and
`onboarding_config`; obsolete fixtures and fallback parsing were removed. The
owner-authorized dev2 removal affects its repository lane only. No live instance
was reset or removed; another instance uses the shared template.

T-85 takes the fail-production-boot option: refused first-boot packs and entry
anomalies propagate their cause through the boot firewall before module boot
writes are persisted. Docs now describe the current game, eight seam messages,
current feeds, deliberation and cockpit screen zero. Strict private-item rustdoc
required the associated 132 documentation/comment fixes. T-54 is comment-only:
per-channel K6 leases still wait for a second station under Q33. CI declares
strict rustdoc, built-SPA release/TLS checks and the cost-run inventory, with an
exact-filter mock-provider step; no paid LLM provider was used.

T-41 uses one deadline covering polling and nested SSH/store reads while keeping
intentional firing cadence. Provisional observer tests select a signed test
sensor/unit pack with a 15-second classification delay; combat fixtures wait for
classified identities. Grace waits observe the exact pilot slot becoming
`left`, preserving reconnect and reflex assertions; abort journals terminate
with `aborted`. Final review also corrected the solo `CONTACTS` wait to retry
commit/control transients and require `No contacts.` or the row's `(rel `
marker. Both solo tests passed after this correction.

their all-target Clippy, formatting and diff checks passed. Separately, the
split-process recovery gate reported two passed and one failed after recovery
succeeded but SSH closed before its final banner. `6463f71d` observes gateway
completion and the exact supervision-abandoned result. These six test-file
corrections through `fbe91f75` preserve production behavior and the original
security/recovery assertions. At `ffa12f6b`, all six corrected targets passed on
Linux: 89 tests across the five workspace targets plus the three-test live-Redis
process-cut matrix. The original failed sweep remains recorded as failed.

Private build artifacts drove the validation host to 100% reported disk use
(115 MiB still free at the lowest observation; no `ENOSPC` observed). The owned
runner/bot were paused; private completed test executables were reclaimed while
source, logs and live paths were retained. Limited subsequent service/journal
checks found no restart or disk-write error; they do not prove absence of every
historical effect. Three bot E2E tests timed out during the pause; the clean
separate bot rerun passed all 262 tests. The
[validation report](../reviews/cut-l-2026-09-22/validation.md)
records the incident, exact cleanup scope, commands and outcomes.

**Final validation:** the frozen Linux aggregate was 31 passed of 34 gates;
all twelve continuation gates at `ffa12f6b` passed. Final arena harness
p50/p95/p99/max was 2.070/14.854/14.998/15.167 ms, above the 12 ms p99 target;
assertions were disabled. All 105 arena and 42 static deterministic report fields
matched the frozen run and earlier Windows baselines. The independently verified
evidence and command/count index are linked from the validation report. Private
Redis shutdown and build-cache removal were verified, restoring 183.0 GiB free
(`df` displayed `184G`); no live instance was deployed, reset or removed. GitHub jobs did not
execute because of billing/spending limits; manual validation is not a green CI
run. Cut L closes five bugs and seventeen debts, plus T-54's comment only;
per-channel leases remain open. B-81 records the retained human billet's
source-reviewed `+focus` stale-context/STARTUP gap, without a runtime full-takeover
claim. B.4 remains outside L; AA.1/AA.2/AA.3 are inherited upstream changes.

## 10. Review (2026-09-16, three independent lenses on Draft 0.1)

Three reviewers read Draft 0.1 of docs 16 and 16b against the tree: an architecture and consistency
lens, a feasibility and sequencing lens, and an adversarial lens. Thirty-five findings; every one is
dispositioned below and, where adopted, folded into Draft 0.2 of both documents. Nothing was rejected
outright; three items are owner questions or deferred.

### Critical

| # | Finding | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | The in-RAM ledger with per-pulse `moved` events would reach 100+ MB in an hour and the custody-in bundle would exceed the 256 KiB record and 16 MiB bundle ceilings, failing the whole match commit (adversarial, architecture) | **Adopted.** Ledger streamed as 16 KiB chunks through the world task to `mush_core::Ledger`; `moved` replaced by `position_summary` every 5 s; `ledger.max_bytes`, `max_unflushed_chunks`, `match.max_duration_ms`; the result record holds the digest and log id; A2 restated as "memory flat with the ledger streamed". Doc 16 §3.1, §4; cut A5, T4 |
| 2 | The arena transmitting frames through `GatewaySink` cannot resolve pilots in the split server (no `SessionManager` there) and a full channel tears down the whole gateway boundary (adversarial, feasibility, architecture) | **Adopted.** Frames are a seam message: latest-wins slots drained by the world task and emitted through its normal output path as `SendTarget::Char`; the arena has no sink; T's acceptance includes the gateway twin. Doc 16 §3.1, §5; cut T4 |
| 3 | One-jump motion tests only the destination cell, so units tunnel through buildings and water at `Quiet` and `Alert` (adversarial, architecture) | **Adopted.** The pulse is a sequence of substeps bounded to one cell of the fastest unit; per-cell tests; the invariant "no unit occupies an untested cell"; the cross-tempo property test crosses an impassable band. Doc 16 §3.1, §3.4; cut A2, A4, A7 |
| 4 | The world's `+map` frame lists every unit in the arena domain by room visibility, and staff see everything (adversarial) | **Adopted.** A deployed arena's domain is excluded from `visible_rooms`, `units_for`, `+map`, `look` and unit listings for every viewer; A1 asserts the observer rule surface by surface. Doc 16 §1, §3.6; cut S3 |
| 5 | The contact ledger cannot be "reused unchanged": it is a durable action-state family the arena cannot write, its ids are owner-derived not viewer-scoped, and the arena would silently create a second identity space (architecture, adversarial) | **Adopted.** Arena contacts are an in-RAM shadow with their own id type minted from `draw(seed, contact:<viewer>:<target>)`, never crossing to the durable family; one byte-identical refusal; the reuse claim restated as vocabulary and projection rules. Doc 16 §3.6, D-16-10; cut S2 |
| 6 | Cut R's re-point list missed eight test targets and four contract tests that import the rulesets (feasibility) | **Adopted.** R8 lists them; the four contract tests are rewrites. |
| 7 | Cut R's gate step omitted the legacy-handler stanzas and pinned baseline, the restriction-lints rows and census, the module-namespace owners rows and edges, two panic-budget files and a CI line (feasibility) | **Adopted.** R9. |

|---|---|---|
| 8 | Queued intents survive a seat release because the seam has no revocation and the arena never learns the current epoch; a pilot fires from a pod they left (adversarial, architecture) | **Adopted.** `Control` message; per-`(unit, channel)` epoch table; authorisation at apply; purge on bump; K's verify lens. Doc 16 §3.1, §3.7; cut A3, T3 |
| 9 | Committing post-panic arena state through custody-out inverts the workspace's panic firewall (adversarial) | **Adopted.** A caught panic voids the match; `CustodyIn{Void}` restores check-out snapshots and commits no arena cell. Doc 16 §3.1; §0.6 |
| 10 | Stranded `deployed` markers after a crash or routine hot restart brick every unit that was in a match; no boot sweep specified (adversarial, architecture) | **Adopted.** The marker carries the check-out snapshot; boot reconciliation in the tactics recovery pass restores, clears and releases; a restart-mid-match test. Doc 16 §3.1; cut T5 |
| 11 | The `deployed` refusal was placed at `UnitAuthorityAdapter::prepare_mutation`, which does not exist on `main` (a Codex-branch name); the real admission sites let `@destroy` and `@unit/damage` through mid-match, and one vanished unit would fail the whole check-in (adversarial) | **Adopted.** Real sites named (`TacticsDestroyGate::check`, `TacticsDetachGate::check`, `unit_damage`, `unit_remove`, `@spatial` moves); check-in per-unit fallible with `custody_lost`. Doc 16 §3.1; cut T2 |

Doc 16 §3.1, §3.3, §3.6 |
| 14 | The lifecycle never named the `Boarding → Running` trigger, had no boarding verb, and put check-out in two different places (architecture) | **Adopted.** `BOARD` verb; the trigger (all seated or `match.board_timeout_ms`); check-out on that transition; pre-custody aborts release slots and pods only. Doc 16 §3.7, §3.8; cut K1, K2 |

Doc 16 §3.3, D-16-6; cut C3, K1 |
| 16 | The plan's harness-on-push CI job contradicts D-H-8 and re-implements `scale_harness`; `ci_gated_test_inventory` would fail unless the target is named in `ci.yml` (feasibility, architecture) | **Adopted as D-16-19.** D-H-8 shape (on demand and scheduled, report-only, `TACSIM_ASSERT=1`); the target named in `ci.yml`; the cost run inside the same target. **Owner question:** if a gating harness in CI is wanted, D-H-8 is superseded and the decision is recorded in D-16-19. Cut H3 |
| 17 | No cut plumbs configuration and deploy files; the live instance and example configs would keep advertising a selector that no longer exists (feasibility) | **Adopted.** Cut G. |
| 18 | The arena is a second intent lane, resolution and RNG beside the shipped `+fire` lane, and the plan's §0.2 forbids exactly that without saying which one dies (feasibility) | **Adopted as D-16-20.** T0 retires `mush-sim::combat`, `tactical_intent` staging, the placeholder resolution, `s9_fire_gate` and the `+fire` stanza; `domaintick` stays for world-side domains with a test that a deployed unit is never in one. |

Doc 16 §4; cut C |

### Confirmed sound by the reviewers, no change

Contextual cockpit verbs on a focused station exist (`CommandReach::Operated`, `resolve_seat`,
`channel_for`) and none of the planned verbs collide with a registered global verb; the `JoinHandle`
and two-shutdown-tail pattern is accurate (`PersistHandles`); `catch_unwind` works because `panic =
"abort"` is deliberately refused by a pinned test; the deletion estimate for the two ruleset crates
(about 63k lines) checks out.

## 11. Risks

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Cut R breaks platform tests that used WoD content as a convenience | R8 re-points, never deletes, every test that proved a platform property |
| The world task's output path becomes the arena's bottleneck at 24 pilots and 500 ms | Frames are latest-wins per pilot and dropped when stale; the harness attaches 12 sessions from the first baseline and measures fan-out |
| Custody races (a pilot leaves the pod during check-out, a staff destroy mid-match) | Check-out is one authoritative action; boarding is locked from `Boarding`; the real admission gates refuse deployed units; check-in is per-unit fallible |
| Rate independence silently violated by a later cut | A7's cross-tempo property test is mandatory for every later cut |
| The ledger stream falls behind the world task | The egress ring is bounded; `Lagged` then `Void` are named outcomes; the harness asserts bytes streamed |
| The 2.56 km ceiling is hit by content before the 10 km path lands | The arena pack is authored at 2.56 km; the 10 km addition is designed in doc 16 §11 and re-run through the harness first |
| The centre's rooms in the atlas-owned pack couple the game to `mush-atlas` content ownership | Acceptable under the single-game direction; the tanks and everything mechanical stay in `crates/tacsim/content` |
